title: @pytest.fixture
summary: Declare reusable test setup that pytest injects by parameter name, and tears down afterwards.
description: Fixtures replace setUp/tearDown with something composable: a test asks for what it needs by naming it as a parameter, and fixtures can depend on other fixtures.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: function, class, module, package or session.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Run every dependent test once per value.

returns: A fixture function; its return value, or what it yields, is injected.

examples.title: Setup and teardown around a yield
Parametrised, so one test becomes several

real_world_usage: Temporary directories via the builtin tmp_path, database sessions rolled back after each test, fake clocks, and prebuilt domain objects.

common_mistakes.fix: Tests then leak into each other and pass or fail depending on order. Keep mutable fixtures function-scoped.

common_mistakes.mistake: return instead of yield when cleanup is needed
common_mistakes.fix: Only the yield form runs teardown.
It hides why a test passes. Prefer explicit parameters.

common_mistakes.mistake: Building elaborate fixtures for simple data
common_mistakes.fix: A literal in the test is clearer than indirection through a fixture.

performance_notes: Broader scopes cost less setup but risk shared state. tmp_path and monkeypatch are cheap; a session-scoped database is the usual real win.
security_notes: Never point a test fixture at a production database or a real credential — fixtures run automatically and destructively.
